sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.authors: Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, et al.
sources.citedFor: Tokens generated one at a time from a prompt (§1); weights persist while KV is allocated per request, and weights plus KV take most GPU memory (§1, Fig. 1); query, key, and value vectors and attention (§2.1, Eq. 2–3); requests, prompts, sequences, the prompt and generation phases, and why keys and values are cached (§2.2); requests share the model weights (§2.3); KV cache size per token, and GPU memory, not compute, usually limiting the batch (§3); reservation and fragmentation waste in prior systems (§3.1, Fig. 2–3); one block table per request for all layers, with no performance difference (§4.1 and its footnote); blocks, block tables, waste limited to the last block, blocks reserved only as a sequence needs them, and the prefill and decoding steps (§4.2–4.3); manually shared prefixes, parallel sampling, beam search, and copy-on-write (§4.4); preemption by recompute or swap (§4.5); kernel overhead (§7.1); recompute vs. swap cost (§7.3); block size ablation, default 16 (§7.2); PagedAttention called "an attention algorithm" (§1); token states use 20.4–38.2% of KV memory in the Orca baselines vs. 96.3% in vLLM (§1, Fig. 2); Orca Max, Pow2, and Oracle baselines (§6.1); 2.2× and 4.3× more concurrent requests than Orca Oracle and Max (§6.2, Fig. 13a); 2–4× throughput at similar latency (abstract, §9); paging may slow compute-bound workloads that are not LLMs (§8). arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180

sources.citedFor: Problem with request-level batching; iteration-level scheduling; selective batching (§3); per-request max-token reservation (§4.2, Alg. 1)

sources.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
sources.authors: Lianmin Zheng, Liangsheng Yin, Zhiqiang Xie, et al.
sources.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37), pp. 62557–62583
sources.citedFor: RadixAttention: radix tree over token sequences, pages of one token, LRU leaf eviction, ref-counted nodes, one memory pool shared by cached and running requests, cache-aware scheduling (§3) — the alternative to block hashing. arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104

sources.title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
sources.authors: Amey Agrawal, Nitin Kedia, Ashish Panwar, et al.
sources.citedFor: Prefill is compute-bound and decode memory-bound (§1, §3.1, Fig. 5); TTFT and TBT defined (§2.4); prefill stalls decode (generation stalls) in prefill-first schedulers (§3.2); pipeline-parallel bubbles (§3.3); chunked prefill plus stall-free batching under a per-step token budget (§4.1–4.2, Alg. 3); the token budget trade-off, chunking overhead included (§4.3). arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02310

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
sources.authors: Joshua Ainslie, James Lee-Thorp, Michiel de Jong, Yury Zemlyanskiy, Federico Lebrón, Sumit Sanghai
sources.citedFor: Converting an MHA checkpoint to fewer KV heads takes extra pre-training (uptraining, §2.1); grouped-query attention: query heads split into groups that each share one key head and one value head; GQA-1 is MQA and GQA-H is MHA (§2.2); fewer KV heads shrink the KV cache and the data loaded per decode step (§1, §2.2). DOI: 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.298. arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245

sources.title: Automatic Prefix Caching (design doc)
sources.citedFor: What prefix caching is and why it saves prefill (L3); V1 prefix cache: block hash = (parent hash, block tokens, extra keys); only full blocks cached; sha256 as the default hash (Note 2); touching hit blocks and evicting on pop (L146–147); free queue with LRU eviction, finished blocks freed in reverse order; ref counts. Rendered: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/

sources.title: vLLM source code
sources.citedFor: Current V1 scheduler and KV cache manager behavior. docs/SIM.md lists the exact files and lines. Also `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` L39–41: fp8 KV is stored as one byte (`torch.uint8`); `vllm/config/cache.py` L71: default block size 16, and L101: default `gpu_memory_utilization` 0.92; `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` L2876–2895: default `max_num_seqs` 1024 on non-A100 GPUs with at least 70 GiB, 256 otherwise.
